comments.content: Remove `it.only` before merging — this will disable all other tests in the ReactDOMForm suite.

This condition change looks suspicious. The added `existingStateHook.next !== null` check assumes a fully-upgraded stateful form fiber always has a subsequent hook. If a form was upgraded but only has a single hook (no `.next`), this will re-run the upgrade path and re-mount hooks, corrupting the hook list. Please verify the invariant that an upgraded form always has `next !== null`, and add a comment explaining why, otherwise consider tracking the upgraded state explicitly rather than inferring it from the hook chain length.
